sections.description: Walks through the patient’s early-onset hyperglycaemia discovered on screening, key historical clues, physical findings, and baseline labs that raised suspicion for monogenic diabetes rather than classic type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
subtopics: Demographics and screening-triggered detection of hyperglycaemia and glycosuria
Symptoms without ketoacidosis: polydipsia, polyphagia, weight loss; absence of acanthosis
Family history pattern consistent with autosomal dominant transmission (multiple first- and second-degree relatives with early-onset diabetes)
Anthropometrics and vitals (BMI 24.6 kg/m2; BP 112/70 mmHg) and implications
Baseline glycaemia: HbA1c 10.2%, FPG 12.4 mmol/L, OGTT 2-hour glucose 19.8 mmol/L
Glycosuria as a clue in HNF1A-MODY (lowered renal glucose threshold)
Lipid profile suggesting possible metabolic syndrome and how rising obesity complicates MODY recognition
Neuropathy screen: severely reduced sudomotor function—interpretation and timing in young-onset diabetes
Initial working diagnosis and rationale for starting insulin plus metformin and DPP-4 inhibitor pending further evaluation

sections.section_title: Differential Diagnosis and Diagnostic Workup for Early-Onset Nonautoimmune Diabetes
sections.description: Details how clinicians distinguished MODY from type 1 and type 2 diabetes using targeted history, antibody testing, β-cell reserve, and decision tools, culminating in genetic testing.
subtopics: Key differentials: type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes, MODY (HNF1A, GCK, HNF4A, HNF1B) and less common monogenic forms
Autoantibody testing strategy: GADA, IA-2A, ZnT8; interpretation of negative results and caveats (seropositive MODY outliers)
β-cell reserve assessment: glucagon-stimulated C-peptide (0.39→0.83 nmol/L) thresholds and how they inform insulin dependence vs MODY suspicion
Clinical features supporting MODY over T1D/T2D: early-onset, nonobese/overweight without insulin resistance stigmata, postprandial hyperglycaemia, glycosuria, strong autosomal dominant family history
Using the Exeter MODY probability calculator: strengths, limitations in non-European populations, and role as a pretest filter
When to order genetic testing: criteria, timing relative to stabilization, and selection of NGS panels
Ancillary testing: microalbuminuria screen (negative), retinal assessment, autonomic testing—what is supportive vs diagnostic
Pitfalls: normal C-peptide early in T1D, under-reported family history, confounding obesity, and overlapping phenotypes

sections.section_title: HNF1A-MODY: Molecular Pathophysiology and Genetic Confirmation
sections.description: Explains how HNF1A variants cause diabetes, the specific novel variant identified, and how pathogenicity was established using ACMG-aligned evidence.
subtopics: HNF1A gene basics: location (12q24), structure (10 exons), tissue expression (liver, kidney, pancreas)
Transcriptional roles relevant to phenotype: regulation of insulin, GLUT2, pyruvate kinase; impact on β-cell development/function
Renal phenotype: reduced SGLT2 expression lowering renal glucose threshold → glycosuria
Progressive β-cell failure in HNF1A-MODY: clinical course from postprandial hyperglycaemia to fasting hyperglycaemia
Novel variant details: c.809A>G (p.N270S), exon 4, DNA-binding domain localization

Pathogenicity assessment: absence in ClinVar/VarSome, segregation with disease, proximity to known pathogenic residues, computational evidence (AlphaMissense 0.995), application of ACMG criteria to reach likely pathogenic/pathogenic classification
Spectrum of HNF1A variants and genotype–phenotype considerations; contrasts with other MODY genes (GCK, HNF4A, HNF1B)
Epidemiology and under-recognition in non-European populations; implications for screening strategies

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Strategy and Course in HNF1A-MODY
sections.description: Outlines initial stabilization, transition to gene-informed therapy, comparative pharmacology for HNF1A-MODY, and outcomes in this patient.
subtopics: Initial management at presentation: rationale for short-term basal insulin plus metformin and DPP-4 inhibitor to control severe hyperglycaemia
Reassessing therapy after workup: stopping insulin once HNF1A-MODY confirmed and β-cell reserve deemed sufficient
Preferred agents in HNF1A-MODY: low-dose sulfonylureas as historical first-line; efficacy and hypoglycaemia risks
GLP-1 receptor agonists as alternatives or preferred in hypoglycaemia-prone patients: evidence from crossover trials vs glimepiride
Role of metformin and DPP-4 inhibitors in insulin-sensitizing and incretin pathways for maintenance therapy
Caution with SGLT2 inhibitors in HNF1A-MODY: pathophysiologic rationale (already lowered SGLT2), risks of dehydration and euglycaemic DKA
Patient’s trajectory: HbA1c 10.2% → 9.1% at 1 month → 6.0% at 6 months on dulaglutide; long-term control on metformin + saxagliptin
Monitoring for complications: microalbuminuria, retinopathy, neuropathy; lifestyle interventions and education

sections.section_title: Clinical Implications, Pitfalls, and Precision Medicine Lessons
sections.description: Synthesizes key takeaways on recognizing MODY, integrating genetics into care, and counseling families, with a focus on avoiding misdiagnosis and optimizing cost-effective testing.
subtopics: Red flags for MODY in clinic: age <35, autosomal dominant family history, nonautoimmune status, glycosuria with modest hyperglycaemia, preserved C-peptide
Stepwise diagnostic algorithm: clinical triage → antibodies → C-peptide → probability calculators → targeted NGS
Interpreting variants beyond databases: using ACMG framework, segregation, domain biology, and computational tools
Therapeutic personalization: when to favor sulfonylureas vs GLP-1RA; deprescribing insulin post-confirmation
Family implications: cascade testing, anticipatory guidance, and reproductive counseling
Health-system considerations: underdiagnosis in diverse populations, building equitable access to NGS, and avoiding unnecessary long-term insulin
Common pitfalls: over-reliance on BMI, false reassurance from single-timepoint C-peptide, and overlooking MODY in seronegative presumed T1D
Key teaching points and exam pearls derived from the case
